description: Tier → concrete model roster. Consumed by tier_matrix.py.
notes: async_threshold_sec — if max timeout_sec across chosen tier meets or exceeds this, tier_matrix.py sets requires_async=true

This matrix is authored against the DIRECT backend (own API keys): gemini-3 + openai-cli. The agy-cli/cliproxy-cli bridges were retired after their ~2026-06-30 expiry; provider_backend.py keeps their translation table for recovery only.

Gemini lane is pinned to 'pro-latest' (= gemini-pro-latest), which resolves to gemini-3.1-pro-preview as of 2026-07-25. The stable alias is preferred over a preview pin per the 3.0 preview-EOL incident (2026-03-09).

Thinking is split by tier because gemini-3.x reasoning depth and latency trade off directly (measured on a hard prompt, 2026-07-25): thinking_level=LOW -> 2,140 thought tokens / 30.0s; HIGH -> 8,473 / 74.8s. deep+ultra buy maximum reasoning; simple+standard stay inside their 60s/120s timeouts.

OpenAI lane runs gpt-5.6-sol with the same tier split. Measured on the same hard prompt (2026-07-25): reasoning low -> 1,024 reasoning tokens / 31.6s; high -> 6,656 / 120.4s; xhigh -> 11,548 / 190.6s. deep uses high (120s of a 240s ceiling); ultra uses xhigh (190s, only safe under the 1800s ceiling). Raising deep to xhigh would need the 240s ceiling raised too.
Do not raise simple/standard to thinking 'high': 74.8s exceeds the simple tier's 60s timeout.
legacy_fallbacks preserves older direct-API defaults (flash/pro/o3) for recovery/reference only.
This matrix is hand-edited by the lead. Workers must not modify without approval.
Timeout ladder alignment (v3.6.1): deep timeout_sec set to 240s to match synod-modes.yaml 'model:240' (safer, smaller ladder chosen). ultra stays 1800s (manual/async-only). simple=60s, standard=120s.
simple tier carries two providers (gemini + openai/gpt54mini) so every tier can run a multi-agent debate. 'fast' is a v3.1 alias for 'simple'; tier_matrix.py normalises it via TIER_ALIASES.
